innkeeper.note: Behind the bar all day and half the night. The one trade with somewhere to be after dark.

seller.note: A market pitch from dawn until the light goes, then the inn. Buys what hunters and farmers bring in.

then.note: The evening at the inn, and it is bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place. A village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never once show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.

farmer.note: Out to the field early and round the herd all morning, back through the square at noon, the field again, the inn of an evening. Badly hurt, the surgery comes first. The cattle are the village's own, off the register, so a village with none simply has him standing in his field as he always did.

then.note: At the field: walk the herd, beast to beast. A village with no cattle falls through to standing in it.
At the field: walk the herd, beast to beast. A village with no cattle falls through to standing in it.

The evening at the inn, and it is bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place. A village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never once show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.

hunter.note: The whole trade in one branch: out to the woods, take something, carry it in, sell it, and spend what it fetched. A mauling sends them to the surgery first.

first.note: Carrying a kill? Then the market, whatever hour it is — meat does not keep.
Coin in the purse and evening drawing in: eat, drink, and buy tomorrow's arrows.
Daylight and nothing on the shoulder: find something.

note: Out to the stand at first light, cut all day, and home at dusk.

The shape is the miner's, because the trade is: a man who walks out of the village to where the material is, works a face all day, and brings nothing back on his shoulder. What he cuts is landed in the village's yard by `builderDay` in `game/interact/builder.ts`, once a day, whether or not anybody was there to watch — exactly as a miner's gold is minted by `game/mines.ts` rather than carried home in his hands. So there is no `take` and no `sell` in here, and that is deliberate: a tree that also made him carry timber to a stall would mint the same wood twice.

`woods` is the post, which is the same one the hunter walks to, and it is the right one for the same reason `heights` is right for the miner: posts are a fact about the village and the stand he is actually cutting is not something `postsOf` knows. He walks to the trees; which tree is his own business.

`dig` is the felling, and the borrowing is honest rather than lazy. `living.ts` explains why a miner's pick is drawn with the sword's `swing` — it is the nearest motion a body in this game actually has — and an axe into a trunk is nearer to it than the pick was. He stands at the stand and swings, which reads from twenty paces up as a man working, which is where this camera watches from.
A longer day than a farmer's and the same as a miner's: the walk out is half of it.

first.note: First light to late afternoon at the trees. `goTo` walks him out and gives way to the saw the moment he is there; `dig` never succeeds, so he holds the stand until the hour changes and this branch stops being true — which is how the miner holds his face all day.

The inn, bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place, and a village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.
And then home, which is the branch the miner's tree was found to be missing: a man with nowhere to go at the end of the day walks the street until sunrise.

constable.note: Trouble first, whatever the hour: an animal on a villager is what the job is for, and somebody the law wants is worse. Otherwise the square, the gate, and the inn.

first.note: A killer the village has had enough of outranks even a wolf: the wolf is only hungry. Forget whatever was marked, walk them down, and take them in once close enough.
Somebody being savaged outranks everything else in the day.

then.note: The evening at the inn, and it is bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place. A village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never once show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.

doctor.note: In the surgery all day. Anybody who comes in gets seen, whether or not they can pay.

soldier.note: The road in and the road out, all day. Somebody has to watch them.

then.note: The evening at the inn, and it is bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place. A village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never once show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.

villager.note: Anybody in a village the register has not given a trade: the elder, whoever keeps the horses, and every face in a street that is only a face. They had no tree at all, so they fell through to the one that drives a wandering animal — which wanders at three in the morning exactly as it does at noon, and is most of why a village at midnight looked like a village at noon.

first.note: The day is spent about the square, which is where somebody with nothing in particular to do is.
An hour at the inn before bed, which is what an evening in a village is.

And in at dark. Every trade in this file ends on this branch and this is the reason: a village where everybody is somewhere by midnight is a village that looks asleep, and the few still out are worth looking at.

hired.note: Bought and paid for. Keep at the shoulder of whoever is paying, and put down whatever goes for anybody near them. The gate can wait until the bargain is done. What he has been told changes which of these he takes, not how he takes it: told to hold he still defends himself, told to fight he still walks round a boulder rather than into it.

first.note: Posted to a tower. He goes to the foot of it, he is on the fighting platform a moment later, and from up there he shoots whatever comes near enough to be worth an arrow. Above the trouble branch on purpose: a bowman who climbs down to go and hit something with his sword is a bowman who has thrown away the only thing a bow is for, and a tower with nobody on it is a tower. He is not safe up there — anything that reaches the foot of it can still be a problem when he steps off — but while he is on it he outranges nearly everything in the country.

steps.note: Wrapped so that a quiet watch still claims the tick. Without it a man with nothing to shoot at falls through to the branch below, which sends him off after whatever is nearest with teeth — and the first wolf a mile away empties the tower.

first.note: Something with teeth on somebody is the whole of what a sword arm is for.
Told to fight: go for what is dangerous rather than waiting for it to go for somebody.
Told to hold: stand where you were put. Whatever comes to him is still his business — the branch above this one is the trouble branch, and it is above for that reason.

then.note: Drop whatever he had marked, and stand where he was put — walking back to the spot if anything shoves him off it. Nothing above this has claimed the tick, so there is nothing on anybody: he is waiting, and waiting somewhere in particular.

first.note: Nothing to fight and nothing said: drop the mark and walk at the hero, which is what following is. `forget` was its own branch here and that was a bug with teeth — `act` returns success and `first` is a selector, so a standing `forget` swallowed every quiet tick and the branch under it was unreachable. A hired man never once walked after anybody; it read as working because a hero who teleports drags his company with him and `muster` re-seats them every half second.

sailor.note: Down at the water when there is water to be down at, and in the inn when there is not.

then.note: The evening at the inn, and it is bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place. A village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never once show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.

climber.note: Up before anybody, on the high ground all day, and back down for supper.

then.note: The evening at the inn, and it is bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place. A village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never once show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.

explorer.note: Never in the same place twice. Ranges further than anybody and comes back with stories.

then.note: The evening at the inn, and it is bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place. A village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never once show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.

facework.note: A shift at the rock face, which is where every coin in this world is minted. Underground only: `src/game/crews.ts` puts the village's miners at the cuts when somebody walks into their mine, and gives each of them a `work` post on the tile he is cutting at. Filed under a name no village trade uses, on purpose — his trade is `miner` and he is called one, but giving this day to the trade itself would put every miner in the country outside his own front door swinging a pick at the grass. No hour in it either: a shift underground does not know what the sky is doing, and a mine you can only find people in between ten and four is a mine you would swear was empty.

steps.note: Back to his own cut if anything has shouldered him off it, and near enough is standing at it.

note: Up to the high ground at first light, back down at dusk, and the inn after.

This is the surface half of a miner's day and it had no tree at all — a villager whose trade is mining fell through to the wanderer and pottered about the square like everybody else, which is why the trade was invisible from the street as well as from underground.

`heights` rather than a mine of his own, and that is a real limitation worth writing down: posts are worked out from the village (`entities/villagers.ts`) and a village's claimed mine lives in `game/mines.ts`, which knows nothing about posts. The highest ground within a ring of the village is where caves are, so it is the right direction and the wrong precision — he walks towards the hills and not to the mouth. Giving `postsOf` the claimed cave would fix it and wants the two to be introduced.
The shift itself is `facework`, which `game/crews.ts` gives him when somebody walks into the workings. This is what he does when nobody is down there to see him.

first.note: First light to late afternoon on the high ground. A longer day than a farmer's, because the walk out is half of it.
The inn, and he has earned it more visibly than most.

then.note: The evening at the inn, and it is bought rather than merely attended: `spend` pays whoever keeps the place. A village whose books credit the innkeeper every day and never once show a coin crossing the bar is an economy happening in the dark.

first.note: And then home, like everybody else above ground. He was the one trade in the village with nowhere to go at the end of the day: the tree ran out after the inn, no branch claimed the tick, and a man who had been down a mine since dawn wandered the street until sunrise. Found by counting who was still out at one in the morning.
